title: Black Loyalist evacuation from New York to Nova Scotia (Book of Negroes), 1783
summary: As British forces left New York in 1783, Sir Guy Carleton had ship inspectors record Black people granted passage in the Book of Negroes: 1,336 men, 914 women and 750 children, about 3,000 in all. Most went to Nova Scotia, founding settlements including Birchtown and Port Roseway (Shelburne); others went to the British West Indies or London.

uncertainty.note: Gotham Center gives the Book of Negroes period as 26 April to 30 November 1783; Wythepedia gives 23 April to 30 November and notes the Kew copy's title spans 23 April to 31 July.

where.modern_name: New York City, USA (port of embarkation; destination Nova Scotia, Canada)
where.historical_name: British-occupied New York City, British North America

importance.justification: Largest organised departure of free Black people from the new United States and the origin of Nova Scotia's Black Loyalist settlements.

related.because: Encyclopedia Virginia says roughly half of the 3,000 African Americans evacuated from Manhattan in 1783 had fled the coast largely because of Dunmore's proclamation.
Wythepedia notes that some of those evacuated to Nova Scotia later migrated to Sierra Leone.
